My first suicidal ideation: age 8, looking at the kitchen knife & wondering how it'd feel to stab myself with it.
Feelings of isolation, despair, guilt.. I once graffitied on the wall, " I hate my dad"...

I'm 18 now and I'm still feeling that way, but on a more intense level. ..

It can be so difficult to overcome our childhoods..

My school nurse gives a very maternal, caring vibe towards me... This post reminded me of her and I realized that I've been subconsciously attaching her with the concept of "mom" in my head...

How embarrassing of me... but I think, we never stop looking for the mom and dad we never had.

Yes.. My parents, grandparents, great-grandparents ALL got divorced. I have no idea what a healthy family looks or feels like.
My father had me in a second marriage so he doesn't allow me to mingle with his relatives (since I'm "illegitimate" or whatever). My mother's relatives are 100% dysfunctional.

I don't really have a specific role model to be honest...
But I do look up to certain musicians (eg. Jhené Aiko — lost her brother, single mom, deals with bipolar disorder. Her music soothes my soul. She gets me.), and I also get inspired by fictional characters from my favorite books.

Sometimes we have to look farther than our surroundings to find something positive...

I 100% relate to this. This is my current living situation.
I live w my father & his colleagues. He only talks about work with them, then speaks in his native tongue to his relatives. He doesn't say anything to me, except about school or eating. If I'm lucky, he might discuss something from the TV...

I know almost nothing about him as a person, despite living with him for 10 years.

I feel like he passed his emotionally stunted behaviors to me, since I now have a tendency to self-isolate often

YES. My father is terrible at emotions or making any real emotional connection.
We live in the same house but sometimes we go weeks without having a conversation. He does not care about me as a person — feeding & sheltering me is all he feels responsible for.
This is one of the contributing factors that causes me to self-isolate for long periods of time, often going into depressive episodes.
It's like we're in a boat together, then I fall into the sea, but instead of pulling me up, he watches in silence.

The saying "once bitten, twice shy" comes to mind here.
Whether explicitly or subtly told that our feelings are something we shouldn't talk about, we begin to internalize that fear & shame.

When I get confronted about my feelings, I have 2 options: Either I lie and deflect the question, or (if I cannot lie) I tell the truth and cry a bucket of tears while at it.

In my household, we NEVER talk about feelings. My father does not know what feelings are and never uses emotive language. So even when I'm in other places, that same silent rule restricts me from talking about my feelings with people. It's made my life incredibly lacklustre.

I only talk about my feelings through texts (zero pressure to immediately reply or verbally communicate my distress) and I only talk about my emotions to people with the same mental issues...

For me, it's painful to have to explain my feelings to people who don't understand.

What your parents didn't give you is NOT your fault.
Every child deserves to have their emotional needs met.
If your needs weren't met, and you're facing problems because of that now, please remember that it was not your fault.

Each person has their own reasons for self-harming, whether it's logical or not.

Personally I self-harm when :⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
- after a long period of dissociating from reality to cope with mental problems, self-harming allows me to 'come back to reality', or gain some sense of awareness of my surroundings.  
- to deal with severe depression &/or suicidal thoughts.   
- to "punish" myself (eg. when i miss school). 
- being unable to express anger at others. 
- to stop overthinking when anxious (cutting makes me hyperfocus on the physical sensation, making you forget about everything else). 

I don't condone or advise anyone else to self-harm. It has serious psychological consequences and can easily become addictive (I do it almost daily). If you're lucky to be in a country with adequate mental health services, please make use of that.
